reference: GNU coreutils od from the reference PATH; the reference command processes the same Bash script and fixture files as the candidate builtin.
coverage: Default octal output including an odd trailing byte
Character escapes, hexadecimal bytes, and stacked formats
Typed little-endian signed and unsigned values with custom line width and decimal offsets
Address radix together with byte skip and byte count
Three fresh redirected-stdin invocations in one Bash process
Multiple named files and address continuity
Bash type/help metadata for the registered builtin
Empty and odd-sized operands, typed groups and line/dedup/string state across file boundaries
Global skip/count, early stop before later operands, exact EOF and beyond-EOF skip
Interleaved shared stdin and named files; recovery around missing paths with status and diagnostics
exclusions: The source documents a custom -s strings mode whose meaning differs from GNU od's -s; it is excluded from GNU parity claims.
Floating-point type formatting, very large offsets, and unusual invalid-option diagnostics are outside this compact suite.

cases.purpose: Check GNU's default octal word format and handling of a final incomplete 16-bit word.
cases.script: printf '\001\002\003\004\005' > bytes; od bytes

cases.purpose: Check ASCII/control-character escapes, hexadecimal byte values, and stacked output under hexadecimal addresses.
Check little-endian 16-bit hex/signed-decimal and 32-bit unsigned formatting, stacked alignment, custom line width, and decimal addresses.
Check that -j advances the displayed address and -N limits the number of dumped bytes.
cases.script: printf '0123456789abcdef' > bytes; od -A x -j 2 -N 5 -t x1 bytes

cases.purpose: Check default suppression of repeated full-width lines and -v's request to print every duplicate.
cases.script: printf 'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA' > bytes; od bytes; od -v bytes

cases.purpose: Check that each invocation reads a fresh redirected stdin stream when the builtin runs repeatedly in one Bash process.
cases.script: printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > bytes; od -An -tx1 < bytes; od -An -tx1 < bytes; od -An -tx1 < bytes

cases.purpose: Check GNU -S string extraction: minimum length, printable-byte boundaries, NUL termination, and suppressed addresses.
cases.script: printf 'xxHello\000ab\000World!\000unfinished' > bytes; od -A n -S3 bytes

cases.purpose: Check GNU od's concatenation of multiple file operands and continuous byte addresses across their boundary.
cases.script: printf '\001\002\003' > first; printf '\004\005' > second; od -A x -t x1 first second

cases.purpose: Check nonzero status and a diagnostic when a relative input file does not exist; diagnostic wording may vary.
cases.script: od absent

cases.purpose: Check that -j skips from the current shared stdin position after Bash read consumes a line.
cases.script:
printf 'first line
SECOND line
third
' > stream; { IFS= read -r first; od -An -c -j 2 -N 6; } < stream

cases.purpose: Check Bash's documented builtin type metadata and that help has an entry for od; this is metadata coverage, not operation coverage.
cases.script: type -t od; help od >/dev/null; printf 'help available\n'

cases.purpose: Concatenate odd byte fragments and an empty middle operand into typed words and stacked output; only the final aggregate word is zero-padded.
cases.script: printf '\001\002\003' > first; : > empty; printf '\004\005\006\007' > second; od -A d -w4 -t x2 -t x1 empty first empty second empty

cases.purpose: Apply -j and -N once to the concatenated byte stream, crossing both operand and output-line boundaries.
cases.script: printf 'abc' > first; : > empty; printf 'defgh' > second; printf 'ijk' > third; od -A x -w4 -j4 -N6 -t x1 first empty second third

cases.purpose: Stop opening operands after the global byte limit is reached; the later missing path must not produce a diagnostic.
cases.script: printf 'abc' > first; od -A x -N2 -t x1 first absent

cases.purpose: Skipping beyond all regular-file bytes is an error with a diagnostic, including with an empty operand.
cases.script: printf 'abc' > first; : > empty; printf 'de' > second; od -j6 -t x1 first empty second

cases.purpose: Repeated complete lines spanning an empty operand share one deduplication state and a single final offset; -v prints them all.
cases.script: printf 'ABCDAB' > first; : > empty; printf 'CDABCD' > second; od -A x -w4 -t x1 first empty second; od -A x -w4 -v -t x1 first empty second

cases.purpose: A GNU NUL-terminated printable string may cross a named-file boundary and an empty operand; its offset is global.
cases.script: printf 'xx\000Hel' > first; : > empty; printf 'lo\000World\000' > second; od -A x -S3 first empty second

cases.purpose: Treat named files, empty files and repeated stdin operands as one byte stream; repeated stdin is not rewound.
cases.script: printf 'ab' > first; : > empty; printf 'cd' > stream; printf 'ef' > last; od -A x -t x1 first - empty - last < stream

cases.purpose: Retain status 1 and diagnostic presence while concatenating readable operands around a missing path.
cases.script: printf 'ab' > first; printf 'cd' > second; od -A x -t x1 first absent second

cases.purpose: Empty streams and a skip exactly at a file boundary emit only the appropriate final aggregate address.
cases.script: printf 'abc' > first; : > empty; od -A x -t x1 empty empty; od -A x -j3 -t x1 first empty

cases.purpose: GNU string offsets include the global skip; the global count can end inside a string and must discard that unterminated run.
cases.script: printf 'xxHe' > first; : > empty; printf 'llo\000World\000' > second; od -A x -j2 -N8 -S3 first empty second

cases.purpose: A zero byte count still opens the first input, reporting a missing first operand with status 1.
cases.script: od -N0 absent
